patients.summary: Former construction foreman on Medicare disability with hypertension, hyperlipidemia and PAD who joins in 2020 as a heavy smoker. Over six years he is diagnosed with severe emphysema, right renal artery stenosis, a benign tracheal papilloma, an ascending colon adenoma with iron deficiency, and stage IIIB squamous NSCLC that progresses with SVC syndrome and brain metastases; an SMA aneurysm is repaired along the way.

documents.author: front desk

Went over membership terms, he's in. New patient appointment set for Mon 9/21 at 9:00, 60 min. Asked him to bring all his pill bottles and the name of the old office so we can send for records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT

53 y/o man transferring care after his previous internist retired. Lives in Easthampton with his wife. Was a construction foreman, out on medical leave now and on Medicare disability with a supplemental plan.

HTN: about 9 years, on HCTZ 25 the whole time, says it has always been fine. No home cuff.
Lipids: atorvastatin 40, been on it 6 or 7 years, no muscle complaints.
PAD: last year his legs started cramping in the calves walking from the truck to the job site, worse on the left. Prior doctor did leg artery testing and told him it was blockage; started baby aspirin. Today he gets about two blocks before the left calf makes him stop, rests a minute and it lets go. No rest pain, no foot sores.

PSH: inguinal hernia repair at 45.
Meds: HCTZ 25 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, ASA 81 daily.
Allergies: none known.
FH: father died of lung cancer at 60. Mother has high BP, 77 and doing well. Uncle on dad's side had colon cancer.
SH: smokes, roughly 2 packs a day since he was 16 or 17. Has never seriously tried to stop. Drinks once or twice a month at most. No other substances.

ROS: no chest pain, no palpitations, no dyspnea he'll admit to, no cough. Bowels regular, no blood.

Exam: well-appearing, smells of smoke. BP and vitals per flowsheet. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, a bit distant. Abdomen soft, nontender, well-healed groin scar. Feet warm, DP pulses faint on the L, palpable on the R; no ulcers. No edema.

A/P
1. Hypertension, controlled on HCTZ. CMP today.
2. Hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin 40. Lipid panel.
3. PAD with stable claudication. Continue ASA and statin. Walking program. Main thing that would help his legs is stopping smoking, told him that plainly.
4. Tobacco: 2 ppd. Not ready to set a date. Offered patch or varenicline; he'll think.
5. Health maintenance: hep C and HIV screen today. Colon screening offered, colonoscopy or stool card; he isn't interested right now. Flu shot given L deltoid.
6. Sending for old records.

RTC 6 months, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, your blood work from Monday is back. Kidney function, potassium, sugar, liver tests and blood count are all normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative, so those are done for good. Cholesterol on the atorvastatin is in an acceptable range for now; we'll keep the same dose. The one thing I'd change is the cigarettes, and I'm here when you're ready.

documents.title: Records from prior internal medicine office
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 41 pages by fax from the patient's previous internist (practice closed; records custodian sent). Abstracted:
- Hypertension listed from 2011, HCTZ 25 mg throughout, office BPs mostly 120s-130s/70s-80s.
- Hyperlipidemia, atorvastatin 40 mg started 2014.
- 2019 note: calf claudication L>R, lower extremity arterial study ordered; result page not included in the packet. Aspirin 81 started.
- Inguinal hernia repair 2012.
- Tdap 04/2016.
- Repeated smoking cessation counseling, declined.
Scanned to media, routed to PCP.

documents.title: Refill request
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Electronic refill request from his pharmacy for HCTZ 25 and atorvastatin 40, old prescriber no longer active. Rewrote both under our PCP, 90-day supply with 3 refills. Aspirin is OTC.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE AWV + problem visit

Health risk assessment reviewed with him: lives with wife in a single-level house, no falls, no hearing complaints, drives. Independent with self-care and errands. Mood good, PHQ-2 0. No advance directive yet; gave him the health care proxy form to fill out with his wife.

Problem: L calf claudication is worse over the winter. Now about one block before he has to stop. R leg only aches with hills. No rest pain, no wounds. Still smoking 2 ppd, "down a little" he says.

Exam: BP ok. L DP/PT not palpable today, R DP faint. Feet warm, cap refill brisk, no skin breakdown. Lungs clear but distant. Heart RRR.

A/P
- PAD, L > R, progressing on aspirin/statin. He wants to know if something can be done, he likes walking. Referral to vascular surgery.
- HTN controlled, continue HCTZ.
- Tobacco: talked again. Not ready.
- Colon screening: declined again.
- COVID vaccine: he's eligible next month, plans to get it at the pharmacy.

Next visit in 6 months.

He thinks he was on a second blood thinner for a while after but has run out and nobody refilled it; he's only on the aspirin now. Meds as listed. No new problems.

A/P

- HTN fine. BMP.
- Flu shot today.
- Smoking: same conversation. He knows.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV, subsequent.

Interval: COVID booster at the pharmacy in November. Legs doing well since the stent. Still 2 ppd. When asked, says he gets winded faster than he used to with carrying things or a flight of stairs, has been that way for some months, figures it's age and the cigarettes. No cough, no chest pain, no leg swelling. Doesn't want testing for it now.

Functional: independent, no falls, hearing and vision fine, driving. HCP form completed, wife is agent, copy scanned.
PHQ-2 0. Alcohol rare.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Lungs with mildly decreased breath sounds throughout, no wheeze. Heart regular. No edema. Pulses: L DP palpable.

Plan:
- Breathlessness: told him I'd like breathing tests if this keeps up; he'd rather wait. Revisit at next visit.
- Tobacco: strongly advised quitting.
- Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months with the nurse.
- Colonoscopy/FIT: still no.
- Fasting lipids and CMP today. Vascular records never came; closed the request.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for second Shingrix. Tolerated first dose with a day of tiredness. Given 0.5 mL IM R deltoid. Observed 15 min, no reaction. Series complete.

orders.order: Pulmonary function tests, complete with lung volumes

documents.title: Office Visit - Dyspnea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: getting short of breath.

HPI: Breathing has slowly gotten worse over about the last year. Now has to stop to catch his breath before he's gone several blocks; used to blame getting older. Wife has an albuterol inhaler and he's been borrowing it some days, thinks it helps a little. Denies cough, denies phlegm, no fever, no chest pain. Legs are fine since the stent. Still smoking about 2 packs a day.

Exam: speaks in full sentences. Lungs: quiet breath sounds throughout, prolonged expiratory phase, no wheeze or crackles. Heart regular. No edema today. SpO2 per flowsheet.

A/P
Progressive exertional dyspnea in a 55 y/o with roughly 80 pack-years. Most likely obstructive lung disease. Full PFTs with lung volumes and a pulmonology consult. Told him not to keep using his wife's inhaler; we'll get him his own once we know what this is.
The best thing for his lungs is to stop smoking now. For the first time he says he's ready. Discussed patch/gum and varenicline; he wants to try on his own first, setting a quit date in two weeks. Will call him.
Flu shot today.

documents.title: Quit check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt as planned. He stopped smoking a week ago today, cold turkey, threw out the cartons. Irritable but managing, chewing sunflower seeds. Declines nicotine replacement for now. PFTs are booked for 10/24 and pulmonary for 10/31. Encouraged; told him to call if he wants patches.

reports.text: Complete pulmonary function study: spirometry before and after bronchodilator, lung volumes by plethysmography. Effort and reproducibility acceptable. FEV1/FVC ratio 55%, reduced. Total lung capacity elevated. Residual volume elevated. Findings indicate an obstructive ventilatory defect with hyperinflation and air trapping.
reports.conclusion: Obstructive defect with hyperinflation and air trapping; FEV1/FVC 55%.

medications.drug: NDA020983 60 ACTUAT albuterol 0.09 MG/ACTUAT Metered Dose Inhaler
medications.sig: Inhale 2 puffs every 4-6 hours as needed for shortness of breath

documents.title: Pulmonary Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 10/31/2022
Referred by: primary care

Reason: shortness of breath, review of pulmonary function testing.

Mr. Hennessey is a 55-year-old former construction foreman who describes a year of slowly progressive breathlessness. At this point several city blocks is his limit before he must stop. He has no cough and brings up no sputum. He has been using his wife's albuterol inhaler intermittently with some relief.

History: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, peripheral arterial disease with a femoral stent. Hernia repair at 45.
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family: father with lung cancer, died at 60; mother hypertensive; paternal uncle with colon cancer.
Social: 80 pack-years; he stopped smoking about four weeks ago. Rare alcohol.

Examination: breath sounds diminished on both sides with a hyperresonant percussion note. Barrel-shaped chest with increased anteroposterior dimension. He uses accessory muscles even sitting quietly. Pulmonic component of S2 is loud. Mild edema at both ankles.

Pulmonary function (10/24/2022): FEV1/FVC 55%. TLC and RV both increased, consistent with hyperinflation and gas trapping.

Impression: severe emphysema, upper lobe predominant, in a heavy former smoker.

Recommendations:
1. Tiotropium soft-mist inhaler, 2 inhalations once daily.
2. Albuterol HFA 2 puffs every 4 to 6 hours as needed; he should stop using his wife's.
3. Congratulated on quitting; continued abstinence is essential.
4. Return to pulmonary clinic as needed or with any change.

Thank you for this referral.
Pulmonary & Critical Care

documents.title: Pharmacy fill history
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pharmacy called to verify an outside prescriber for a 90-day supply on file. Fill history shows new tiotropium inhaler and albuterol HFA dated 10/31, written by pulmonology. We have no pulmonary note yet. Called patient: he says the lung doctor told him he has emphysema and to use the new inhaler every morning. Added both inhalers to his list as outside meds. Requested the consult note.

You should hear from the pharmacy in a few days. Keep using it every morning in the meantime; you have enough from the first fill.

documents.title: Prior authorization

documents.body: PA for tiotropium approved through 11/2023. Pharmacy notified, pt notified by voicemail.

documents.title: Pulmonary consult received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Pulmonary letter from 10/31 finally in. Severe upper-lobe emphysema, FEV1/FVC 55%, hyperinflation. On tiotropium plus PRN albuterol. Problem list updated. Will see him in January.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: First visit since the pulmonary consult. Still not smoking, 3.5 months now, proud of it. Uses tiotropium every morning, albuterol maybe twice a week. Breathing a little better than in the fall. Brought a wrist cuff his wife bought: home numbers have been 180s over 90s for a while, he thinks since around Thanksgiving. No headache, no chest pain, no vision change. Taking HCTZ every day.

O: BP 184/96 repeated after 10 min, similar. Lungs diminished bilaterally, hyperresonant, no wheeze. Heart regular, P2 loud. Trace ankle edema.

A/P
- BP well above goal, new since the fall. Could be the quit (weight, stress) or the cuff; asked him to check his cuff against ours and keep a twice-daily log for a month. BMP today. Return in 4-5 weeks; if it's still this high we'll add a second medicine.
- Emphysema stable on tiotropium. Pulmonary letter reviewed.
- Tobacco: abstinent, reinforced.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

orders.reason: progressively worsening hypertension after years of control

documents.title: Office Visit - Hypertension
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Home log reviewed (cuff checked against ours, within 4 points): systolics nearly all 180-190, diastolics mid-90s to 100, both morning and evening. Today 186/98. Asymptomatic.

He had years of good control on HCTZ alone and this is a clear change over the last few months. Differential includes post-quit weight gain (none on the scale, actually), NSAIDs (denies), and a secondary cause given his vascular disease.

Plan:
- Add lisinopril 20 mg daily, keep HCTZ 25.
- BMP in 2 weeks for potassium and creatinine, order in.
- Referral to cardiology given the abrupt worsening and his PAD; would value their take on renovascular causes.
- Call with home readings in 2 weeks.

documents.title: Lab reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: BMP ordered 2/27 still not drawn. LVM for pt to come in any weekday morning, no appointment needed.

documents.title: Lab reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Second message left re: overdue BMP. Cardiology appointment confirmed for 5/11.

documents.title: Cardiology Consultation
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
CARDIOVASCULAR CONSULTATION
Visit date: May 11, 2023

Thank you for asking us to see Mr. Hennessey, 56, for blood pressure that has been climbing.

He has carried a diagnosis of hypertension for 12 years and for most of that time hydrochlorothiazide alone kept it in range. Over roughly the last six months his systolic readings have run 180 to 190, enough that a second agent was recently added by his primary physician. He reports no headaches, no palpitations and no muscle weakness.

Other history: hyperlipidemia; peripheral arterial disease with a femoral artery stent placed two years ago; severe upper lobe predominant emphysema, diagnosed last fall. He is a former smoker of 80 pack-years who quit in October. Alcohol 1 to 2 drinks a month. Off work on medical leave from construction.

Medications per our intake: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, inhalers.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father lung cancer (died 60), mother hypertension, paternal uncle colon cancer.

Laboratory: serum creatinine 1.7 mg/dL against a prior baseline of 1.0. Plasma renin activity is markedly elevated.

Assessment: abrupt loss of control of long-standing hypertension in a patient with diffuse atherosclerosis, a rise in creatinine and high renin. This is renal artery stenosis until shown otherwise.

Plan:
- Renal artery duplex ultrasound.
- Continue the current regimen for now; we will review after the duplex.
- Repeat basic metabolic panel after imaging.

Cardiology

documents.title: Cardiology letter reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Cardiology note reviewed. Creatinine 1.7 from 1.0, renin markedly high, suspected renal artery stenosis, duplex pending. Their med list leaves off the lisinopril I started in Feb; he is taking it per his wife. Called pt, explained, keep both BP meds for now and stay off ibuprofen. Will do labs after the duplex.

reports.text:
RENAL ARTERY DUPLEX ULTRASOUND
Indication: worsening hypertension, rising creatinine.
Technique: grayscale, color and spectral Doppler of the abdominal aorta, both main renal arteries and both kidneys.
Findings: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber. Right main renal artery: elevated velocities with post-stenotic turbulence, consistent with stenosis of 60% or greater. Left main renal artery: normal velocities without significant stenosis. Right kidney and left kidney are normal in size with normal cortical thickness. No hydronephrosis. Intrarenal waveforms are present on both sides.
reports.conclusion: Right renal artery stenosis of 60% or greater. Left renal artery without significant stenosis. Kidneys normal in size.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Note
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Addendum to May consultation.

Renal artery duplex 5/25: right renal artery stenosis of at least 60%; left renal artery without significant narrowing; normal kidney sizes.

Impression: atherosclerotic right renal artery stenosis. Our recommendation is medical management: continue lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide, continue aspirin and statin, and follow creatinine and potassium closely. If blood pressure cannot be controlled or kidney function declines further we will reconsider. Please send us his next metabolic panel.

Cardiology

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 1.4, down from 1.7 at cardiology. Potassium normal. Faxed to cardiology. Recheck at August visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here for BP and kidney follow-up after cardiology's renal artery workup.

Since May he's joined a free program at the senior center: mostly plant-based eating, group walks three mornings a week. Down a few pounds. Home BPs now 140s/80s. Taking lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 daily, no cough, no dizziness. Breathing about the same; albuterol a couple of times a week. Not smoking.

BP 146/88. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. RRR. No edema.

A/P
- Right renal artery stenosis, medical management per cardiology. BMP today.
- HTN improving, not at goal. Program is helping; no med change today, recheck in 3 months.
- Emphysema stable.
- Flu/COVID/pneumonia vaccines this fall, nurse visit in October.

documents.title: BMP result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Creatinine 1.2, continuing to settle. K normal. Copy to cardiology. Portal note sent to patient.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (L deltoid), PCV20 (R deltoid) and updated COVID (R deltoid, 1 inch below PCV20) per PCP standing order for COPD. No prior pneumococcal vaccine in records. Screening negative. Watched 15 min, felt fine, went home.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up, six months out from cardiology's renal artery evaluation. Feels well, nothing new to report.

Still doing the senior-center program: plant-forward meals at home and group exercise. Down 10 lb since May and pleased about it. He brought a newspaper clipping about a study that followed people in a lifestyle program like his and found fewer strokes among them; he's skeptical and wanted my opinion. We talked through it: that kind of study watches people who chose the program, and people who choose it tend to differ in lots of ways (they may smoke less, see doctors more), so it can show an association but can't prove the program caused the difference; a randomized trial is what answers that. Told him the habits are worth keeping regardless, for his BP, his legs and his lungs.

Meds: HCTZ 25, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, tiotropium daily, albuterol PRN.
No smoking since October 2022.

Exam: BP 138/86. BMI 27. Lungs diminished bilaterally, no wheeze. Heart regular. Extremities without edema, pulses palpable.

Labs this morning (fasting): TC 190, HDL 40, LDL 120, TG 150, glucose 98, creatinine 1.1.

A/P
- HTN: much better, near goal. Same regimen.
- R renal artery stenosis: creatinine back to 1.1. BMP in 6 months.
- Hyperlipidemia: continue atorvastatin 40.
- PAD: walking well.
- Emphysema: stable.
- RTC 4-6 months.

documents.title: cholesterol
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doc, my wife wants to know if the cholesterol went down with all the vegetables. I forgot to ask friday.

documents.title: RE: cholesterol
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Sean, total 190 and LDL 120, which is about where it was when you joined, and your fasting sugar was 98, normal. The weight and the blood pressure are where we're really seeing the payoff. Kidney number is also back to 1.1. Keep at it.

documents.title: Prior authorization renewal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Tiotropium PA expiring this month. Renewal submitted with the pulmonary letter and PFT. Approved 11/29 for 12 months; pharmacy aware.

documents.title: Appointment cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt cancelled this afternoon's appt, driveway iced in. Offered next week, he'd rather wait till spring since he's feeling ok. Recall set for April.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Lungs are hyperexpanded with flattened hemidiaphragms and increased retrosternal air space, consistent with emphysema. No focal consolidation, mass or pleural effusion. Heart size normal. Mediastinal contours unremarkable. No acute osseous abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Hyperinflation consistent with emphysema. No mass, infiltrate or effusion.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Hoarseness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: voice gone gravelly, coughing.

HPI: About 7 weeks of a rough voice, a dry cough, and breathing that has gotten noticeably harder, more than his usual. No fever, no weight loss, no night sweats, no sputum, no blood. Not smoking. Using albuterol most days now; it doesn't help much.

Exam: voice hoarse. No neck masses or adenopathy. Lungs: diminished throughout as before, no wheeze, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

CXR today: hyperinflation, no mass.

A/P
Progressive dyspnea with hoarseness and cough in a man with severe emphysema and 80 pack-years. Not typical of a COPD flare; hoarseness this long needs a look at the airway. Expedited pulmonology referral, they can arrange laryngoscopy/CT as they see fit. Call me if worse before then.
Flagged for front desk to push the pulmonary appointment.

documents.title: Your chest x-ray
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sean, the chest x-ray shows the emphysema we already know about and nothing new, no mass or pneumonia. I still want the lung specialists to look at your airway because of the voice. Their office should call you this week.

reports.text: Spirometry with flow-volume loop. Effort adequate. The flow-volume loop shows flattening of both the inspiratory and the expiratory limbs, a pattern of fixed central airway obstruction, superimposed on the known obstructive defect.
reports.conclusion: Flattened inspiratory and expiratory limbs: fixed upper airway obstruction.

documents.title: Pulmonary Follow-up Consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY & CRITICAL CARE
Visit: 05/10/2024

Mr. Hennessey returns, known to us for severe upper lobe predominant emphysema. For three months his breathing has steadily worsened, his voice has become hoarse and he has developed a cough. He has had no fever, no weight loss and no night sweats.

Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, tiotropium, albuterol as needed. NKDA. Former smoker, quit 10/2022.

Examination: audible stridor on both inhalation and exhalation. The voice is coarse and raspy. No cervical or supraclavicular lymph nodes are palpable.

Flow-volume loop today: both the inspiratory and expiratory limbs are flattened.

Impression: fixed central (tracheal) airway obstruction. In this setting a tracheal neoplasm is the leading concern.

Plan: CT of the chest this week, then bronchoscopic evaluation and treatment with our interventional team depending on the CT. He was told to go to the emergency department for any worsening of his breathing.

Pulmonary & Critical Care

reports.text:
CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST
Indication: stridor, fixed airway obstruction on flow-volume loop.
Findings: Polypoid intraluminal soft tissue mass arising from the wall of the mid trachea, measuring about 1.8 cm, narrowing the tracheal lumen by about 50%. No extension outside the tracheal wall. Main bronchi patent. Upper lobe predominant centrilobular and paraseptal emphysema. No pulmonary mass or nodule. No consolidation or effusion. No enlarged mediastinal, hilar or axillary lymph nodes. Heart normal in size; no pericardial effusion. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: 1.8 cm polypoid mid-tracheal mass with about 50% luminal narrowing. Upper lobe predominant emphysema. No lung mass or adenopathy.

documents.title: CT result
documents.author: patient
documents.body: they found a growth in my windpipe. they are going to take it out with a scope june 3. does that mean cancer?

documents.title: RE: CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sean, I saw the CT too. There is a growth inside the windpipe that explains the voice and the noisy breathing. We don't know yet what kind it is; some of these are benign. Removing it with the scope both treats the narrowing and tells us exactly what it is. I'm glad they're moving quickly. Call me anytime before then, and go to the ER if your breathing gets worse.

conditions.label: Benign neoplasm of trachea (squamous papilloma), excised

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: trachea, mid, mass, excision via rigid bronchoscopy.
Gross: multiple tan-pink fragments of soft tissue, aggregate 1.9 x 1.2 x 0.6 cm.
Microscopic: papillary fronds lined by mature squamous epithelium over fibrovascular cores. No dysplasia. No invasive carcinoma.
reports.conclusion: Squamous papilloma of the trachea. Negative for dysplasia and malignancy.

documents.title: Pathology received
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Path from 6/3 rigid bronch: tracheal squamous papilloma, benign, no dysplasia. Called Sean with the result; he and his wife very relieved. Voice already better. Op note not received; requested.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Two weeks after rigid bronchoscopy with removal of the tracheal growth (benign squamous papilloma on path). Went home the same evening. Sore throat for 3 days, now fine. Voice close to normal; wife says he sounds like himself. The noisy breathing is gone and his walking tolerance is back to where it was last year. Cough nearly gone. Still on tiotropium, albuterol rarely.

Exam: voice mildly husky. No stridor at rest or with deep breaths. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. Heart regular.

A/P
- Tracheal papilloma, excised. Pulmonary to arrange airway follow-up; we never got their procedure note, re-requested.
- Emphysema at baseline.
- HTN/renal artery stenosis: BMP today (due).
- Next visit in the fall with the flu shot.

documents.title: refills
documents.author: patient
documents.body: need refills on the blood pressure pills and the cholesterol one. same pharmacy

documents.title: RE: refills
documents.author: RN

documents.title: Office Visit - Fatigue
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: For about three months he's been more and more tired, and gets winded on exertion sooner than he did in the summer. He's lost 10 lb without trying (not on the program anymore, eating normally). No fever, no night sweats. Bowels unchanged, no black or bloody stools he's noticed. Voice fine, no stridor, no cough. Not smoking.

O: Wt 83 kg (87.5 last year). Pale. Lungs diminished as before. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses. No adenopathy.

A/P
Fatigue, exertional dyspnea and unintentional weight loss, looks pale. CBC, iron studies, BMP today. Low threshold for a hematology/oncology consult depending on results. Flu shot given.

documents.title: Anemia results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hgb 9.2, MCV 72, ferritin 15, iron 30, TIBC 450. Microcytic iron deficiency anemia, new (normal on prior counts). With the weight loss this needs a source. Placed hematology/oncology referral, urgent. Called pt; told him we need to find where he's losing blood and that he'll likely need a colonoscopy.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Consultation
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of visit: November 11, 2024

Reason for referral: anemia.

HPI: Mr. Hennessey is 57 and has severe upper lobe predominant emphysema; earlier this year he was evaluated for a tracheal lesion, removed in June. Over the past three months he has become progressively fatigued and short of breath with exertion, and he has lost about 10 pounds without intending to. He denies fevers, sweats at night, or any change in his bowel pattern.

PMH: hypertension, hyperlipidemia, peripheral arterial disease, renal artery stenosis, emphysema, tracheal papilloma (resected).
Medications: hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, aspirin 81 mg, tiotropium, albuterol.
Allergies: none known.
Family: father lung cancer; paternal uncle colon cancer; mother hypertension.
Social: former smoker.

Exam: pale with conjunctival pallor. Stool guaiac positive on rectal examination.

Labs (10/21/2024): hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL (13.8-17.2), MCV 72 fL (80-96), ferritin 15 ng/mL (24-336), serum iron 30 mcg/dL (65-176), TIBC 450 mcg/dL (250-450).

Assessment: microcytic anemia from iron deficiency with occult GI blood loss. A colorectal neoplasm must be excluded.

Plan:
1. Ferrous sulfate 325 mg by mouth daily.
2. Referral to gastroenterology for colonoscopy, ideally within the next few weeks.
3. Follow-up in our clinic in about six months with CBC.

Hematology & Oncology

conditions.label: Colorectal neoplasia
conditions.note: 30 mm ascending colon tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, resected by EMR

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
Specimen: ascending colon polyp, endoscopic mucosal resection, piecemeal; resection base margins submitted separately.
Gross: multiple tan polypoid fragments, aggregate 3.1 x 2.4 x 0.8 cm.
Microscopic: tubulovillous adenoma with areas of high-grade dysplasia. No invasive adenocarcinoma identified. Margin fragments free of adenoma.
reports.conclusion: Tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, ascending colon. No invasive carcinoma. Margins clear.

documents.title: Colonoscopy Report
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
COLONOSCOPY
Date: 12/2/2024
Indication: iron deficiency anemia, guaiac-positive stool.
Sedation: monitored anesthesia care.
Preparation: good.

Findings:
- Cecum reached, appendiceal orifice and ileocecal valve identified.
- Ascending colon: 30 mm sessile polyp with a granular surface. Lifted with injection and removed by endoscopic mucosal resection in several pieces. Base inspected, no residual tissue. Clips placed to close the defect.
- No other polyps or masses. No diverticula. Rectum normal on retroflexion.

Impression: large ascending colon polyp, resected; likely source of chronic blood loss.
Recommendations: await pathology. Continue iron. Surveillance colonoscopy in 6 months to check the resection site.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Colon pathology
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Colon polyp path: tubulovillous adenoma with high-grade dysplasia, no cancer, margins clear. Called Sean. Explained it was precancerous and is out, and the 6-month scope matters. Added to problem list.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Follow-up of iron deficiency anemia after colonoscopy. Colon polyp (precancerous, high-grade dysplasia) was removed 12/2; GI wants a look at the site in about 6 months. Taking ferrous sulfate daily, dark stools expected, mild constipation managed with prunes. Energy noticeably better, walks his neighborhood loop again. Weight steady. No bleeding. Breathing at baseline, voice normal.

Exam: less pale. Lungs diminished, no stridor. Heart regular. Abdomen benign.

CBC today.

A/P
- Iron deficiency anemia, improving on oral iron; continue. Heme visit in May.
- Colon adenoma: surveillance colonoscopy around June, reminded him.
- HTN on lisinopril/HCTZ, home BPs 130s.
- Emphysema stable.

Video, pt at his kitchen table, wife beside him.

Cough since early February, bringing up yellowish phlegm most mornings. No fever, no blood, no chest pain. Breathing maybe slightly worse; using albuterol a bit more. Not smoking. Eating fine but jeans looser.

Looks comfortable on video, speaking in full sentences, no audible stridor, voice normal.

documents.title: Hematology/Oncology Follow-up
documents.author: hematology/oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit: 5/5/2025

Mr. Hennessey returns for follow-up of iron deficiency anemia (ascending colon adenoma removed in December). The anemia has corrected on oral iron. New since his last visit is a cough, now about three months, bringing up yellowish sputum, and further weight loss. No fevers, no night sweats, no blood in the sputum.

Vitals: BP 145/90, pulse 88, respirations 18.
Exam: breath sounds reduced at the right base with dullness to percussion there. No adenopathy.

Labs today: hemoglobin 13.5, WBC 7,500, platelets 250,000, sodium 140, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.0, fasting glucose 100.

Chest radiograph today: mass in the right lower lobe.

Assessment:
1. Right lower lobe lung mass in a former heavy smoker; malignancy until proven otherwise.
2. Iron deficiency anemia, resolved. Continue ferrous sulfate for now.

Plan: referral to pulmonology for bronchoscopy with biopsy, requested urgently. We will see him again once tissue is back.

Hematology & Oncology

conditions.label: Non-small cell lung cancer, right lower lobe

reports.text:
SURGICAL PATHOLOGY
A. Right lower lobe endobronchial mass, forceps biopsies: non-small cell carcinoma, squamous cell type (p40 positive, TTF-1 negative).
B. Lymph node, station 4L, EBUS-guided needle aspiration: metastatic squamous cell carcinoma.
C. Lymph node, station 4R, EBUS-guided needle aspiration: metastatic squamous cell carcinoma.
D. Lymph node, station 7, EBUS-guided needle aspiration: benign lymphoid tissue, no malignancy.
Molecular testing sent separately.
reports.conclusion: Squamous cell carcinoma of the right lower lobe, non-small cell type, with metastasis to station 4R and contralateral station 4L lymph nodes.

documents.title: Bronchoscopy with EBUS
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
FLEXIBLE BRONCHOSCOPY WITH ENDOBRONCHIAL ULTRASOUND
Date: 5/19/2025
Indication: right lower lobe mass.
Anesthesia: general, laryngeal mask airway.

Findings: vocal cords move normally. Trachea: the prior papilloma resection site in the mid trachea is smooth with no recurrent lesion. Carina sharp. Left bronchial tree normal. Right lower lobe: friable endobronchial tumor partly occluding the basal segments; forceps biopsies taken.
EBUS: stations 4R, 4L and 7 sampled by needle aspiration.

Complications: none. Discharged home the same day.

Pulmonary & Critical Care

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - Lung Cancer Diagnosis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with his wife after the biopsy showed squamous cell lung cancer in the right lower lobe with cancer in lymph nodes on both sides of the chest (EBUS 4R and 4L). PET-CT is tomorrow, brain MRI Thursday, thoracic oncology next Monday.

He wanted to know whether quitting in 2022 had been for nothing; told him it wasn't, it's helped his heart, legs and lungs and will help him get through treatment. His father died of lung cancer at 60 and he keeps coming back to that. Sleeping poorly the last week. Not depressed by screen; worried, which is fair.

Cough continues, some yellow sputum, no blood. Breathing at baseline.

Exam: tired but well. Lungs diminished, reduced at R base. Heart regular. No edema.

Meds reconciled: HCTZ 25, lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, tiotropium, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 daily.

Advance care planning (35 min with patient and wife): health care proxy on file, wife is agent, he confirms. He wants all treatment the oncologists recommend. Not ready to talk about what he'd want if treatment stops working; open to it later. MOLST not completed today.

A/P
- NSCLC, squamous, RLL with mediastinal nodes. Staging underway. I'll coordinate and see him between oncology visits.
- Everything else stable, no changes.

conditions.label: Non-small cell lung cancer, right lower lobe

documents.title: Thoracic Oncology Consultation
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
THORACIC ONCOLOGY - NEW PATIENT
Date: June 2, 2025

Diagnosis: squamous cell carcinoma of the right lower lobe.

Staging:
- PET-CT 5/28/2025: 4.6 cm FDG-avid right lower lobe mass; FDG-avid right hilar and bilateral mediastinal lymph nodes; no distant metastatic disease. No pleural effusion.
- MRI brain with and without contrast 5/29/2025: no intracranial metastasis.
- EBUS 5/19: 4R and 4L positive, station 7 negative.
- Molecular: no EGFR, ALK or ROS1 alteration.
Stage: T2b N3 M0, stage IIIB. Not a surgical candidate.

Performance status: ECOG 1.
Comorbidities noted: severe emphysema, hypertension, PAD with femoral stent, right renal artery stenosis, prior tracheal papilloma and colon adenoma.

Recommendation, discussed at length with Mr. Hennessey and his wife: definitive concurrent chemoradiation with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel and thoracic radiation to 60 Gy in 30 fractions, followed by consolidation durvalumab for up to a year. Simulation with radiation oncology this week; planned start 6/9.

Oncology

Diagnosis: stage IIIB (T2b N3 M0) squamous cell carcinoma, right lower lobe.
Treatment: 6/9/2025 - 7/18/2025. Right lower lobe primary, right hilar and bilateral mediastinal nodes, 60 Gy in 30 fractions, IMRT, with concurrent weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel by medical oncology.

Tolerance: completed as planned with no treatment breaks.

Follow-up: medical oncology to begin consolidation durvalumab; radiation oncology follow-up with imaging in 3 months.

Three weeks out from finishing chemoradiation (last fraction 7/18). Still tired by mid-afternoon, naps. Appetite coming back slowly; down to 79 kg. Cough less, sputum clear now. Using albuterol a few times a week. Durvalumab infusions to start later this month.

BP 132/80. Lungs diminished, fewer sounds R base. Skin over the radiation field intact. Heart regular. No edema.

- Anemia: Hgb 12.6 after chemo, ferritin 88 so iron stores are fine. Stop the ferrous sulfate.
- HTN: on target. Same regimen.
- Weight: protein shakes, small frequent meals.
- Colon surveillance scope: was due in June, put off during treatment; GI will reschedule with oncology's input.
- Flu and COVID shots in the fall if oncology agrees.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
On durvalumab every 4 weeks since 8/25 (two infusions so far); we didn't have that on his list until today. Tolerating it: no rash, no diarrhea, no new cough. Energy better than in August. Eating more, weight stable at 78. Walking twice a day.

BP fine. Lungs diminished, no crackles. Heart regular. Skin clear. No edema.

reports.text:
CT ANGIOGRAPHY ABDOMEN
Indication: abdominal pain, pulsatile abdominal mass.
Technique: arterial and venous phase imaging after IV contrast with multiplanar reconstructions.
Findings: Saccular aneurysm arising from the proximal superior mesenteric artery just distal to its origin from the aorta, measuring 3.8 cm in maximal diameter, projecting posteriorly. No surrounding hematoma or extravasation. The SMA beyond the aneurysm opacifies normally. Celiac axis and inferior mesenteric artery patent. Abdominal aorta normal in caliber. Liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys unremarkable apart from known renal arteries. Bowel normal in caliber without wall thickening. No ascites.
reports.conclusion: 3.8 cm saccular aneurysm of the proximal superior mesenteric artery, projecting posteriorly. No rupture.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Arrival 11/12/2025 11:40

Chief complaint: abdominal pain.

HPI: 58-year-old man with stage IIIB lung cancer on immunotherapy. For about three months he has had a dull, vague abdominal ache that comes and goes, more likely after he eats, sometimes going through to his back. No nausea, vomiting or diarrhea; no blood in the stool. His wife also points out that his face and neck have looked puffy for about a week.

Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, albuterol, durvalumab.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: in no distress. Face and neck appear full, neck veins distended. Lungs diminished. Abdomen: a pulsatile mass is felt in the central abdomen; it is not tender. Bowel sounds normal. No guarding.

CTA abdomen: 3.8 cm saccular proximal SMA aneurysm projecting posteriorly, no rupture.
CT chest: SVC narrowed by enlarging right paratracheal nodal tissue.

ED course: hemodynamically stable. Vascular surgery and interventional radiology consulted. Admitted to medicine.

Disposition: admitted.

conditions.label: Superior vena cava syndrome secondary to lung cancer

reports.text:
CT CHEST WITH CONTRAST
Indication: facial swelling, known right lower lobe lung cancer after chemoradiation.
Findings: Enlarging soft tissue in the right paratracheal region compared with the staging study, consistent with nodal disease, narrowing the superior vena cava. Treated right lower lobe mass with post-radiation change. Emphysema. No pleural effusion. Prior tracheal resection site unremarkable; trachea patent.
reports.conclusion: Superior vena cava narrowing from enlarging right paratracheal nodal disease.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 11/12/2025  Discharged: 11/15/2025

Principal diagnoses:
1. Superior vena cava syndrome due to progression of stage IIIB squamous NSCLC (right paratracheal nodes).
2. Saccular aneurysm of the proximal superior mesenteric artery, 3.8 cm, symptomatic.

Course:
Admitted from the ED. CT chest showed the SVC narrowed by enlarging right paratracheal nodal disease, explaining a week of facial and neck swelling. Interventional radiology placed an SVC stent on 11/13 through the right femoral vein without complication; swelling largely resolved by the next morning.
Vascular surgery evaluated the SMA aneurysm. Given its size and his symptoms they recommend elective endovascular repair after he recovers from this admission, to be scheduled in their clinic.
Oncology saw him in hospital: this represents progression on durvalumab, which is stopped. Second-line therapy to be discussed in clinic.

Discharge medications: unchanged home medications (lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, tiotropium, albuterol). Durvalumab discontinued.

Follow-up: primary care within 1-2 weeks; oncology 11/20; vascular surgery 12/3.

Hospital Medicine

documents.title: Discharge summary received
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: Call from wife
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's wife called: he's been in the hospital since Wed. Went in for the belly pain, they found an aneurysm on an intestinal artery, and also the cancer is pressing on the big vein in his chest, which is why his face was swollen. They put a stent in the vein yesterday and the swelling is much better. Expected home tomorrow. Booked post-hospital visit 11/24 with PCP. Will request records.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit. Spoke with wife by phone 11/14; discharge papers she brought reviewed today (summary not yet received from the hospital).

Hospitalized 11/12-11/15. Abdominal pain led to a CT showing a 3.8 cm aneurysm of the superior mesenteric artery. Also found SVC syndrome from growing lymph nodes in the chest; SVC stent 11/13. Oncology says the cancer has progressed and has stopped durvalumab; they're discussing next treatment at his 11/20 visit (he says chemo every 3 weeks starting in December). Vascular plans a stent-graft repair of the aneurysm, consult 12/3.

Now: face and neck back to normal. Still a mild ache after meals, no worse. Bowels normal, no blood. Breathing at baseline.

Exam: no facial or arm swelling, neck veins flat, R groin access site healed. Lungs diminished. Abdomen soft, pulsatile midline mass, nontender. No edema.

Meds reconciled: durvalumab off. Others unchanged.

A/P
- SVC syndrome, stented, resolved.
- SMA aneurysm, symptomatic, repair planned by vascular. Return precautions for severe or sudden pain.
- NSCLC with nodal progression; second-line therapy per oncology.
- HTN, renal artery stenosis: BMP today.
- Will see him again before the repair.

Started docetaxel every 3 weeks on 12/8, two cycles so far; adding it to his list now. Tired for a few days after each infusion. No fevers. Vascular repair of the SMA aneurysm booked for 1/21, endovascular through the groin; they told him to stay on aspirin.

Abdominal ache after meals continues, same as before, no weight loss beyond what we know. Face/neck swelling has not come back.

One month after endovascular repair of the SMA aneurysm (1/21, one night in hospital). The after-meal belly pain is gone, first time in months. Groin healed. Vascular sees him with a CT in March. We still have no operative note.

Docetaxel continues every 3 weeks; tired for a few days after each one, then OK. Appetite fair. Not smoking.

Exam: Lungs diminished. Abdomen soft, nontender, no pulsatile mass felt. R groin healed, no hematoma or bruit. Pedal pulses present.

VASCULAR SURGERY CLINIC
Date: 3/9/2026

Seen seven weeks after endovascular exclusion of a 3.8 cm saccular proximal SMA aneurysm with a covered stent (1/21/2026). Postprandial pain has resolved. Access site healed.

CTA today: stent graft patent, aneurysm excluded, no endoleak.

EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Arrival 5/2/2026 07:50 by ambulance.

Chief complaint: seizure.

HPI: 59-year-old man with stage IIIB squamous NSCLC on docetaxel and a history of SVC syndrome (stented). His wife found him having a seizure in bed this morning. No prior seizures. She says he has complained of a headache for two weeks that over-the-counter pain relievers have not touched, and that he has been forgetting things and groping for words in conversation.

Meds: lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin, aspirin, tiotropium, albuterol, docetaxel.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vital signs stable. Drowsy and slow to answer, consistent with the postictal state; oriented by the end of his stay here. No focal neurologic deficit: pupils equal and reactive, face symmetric, strength and sensation equal, no drift. Tongue without laceration.

MRI brain: multiple well-circumscribed lesions at the gray-white junction with vasogenic edema, consistent with metastases.

ED course: levetiracetam load, dexamethasone. No further seizure. Admitted to medicine with neuro-oncology and radiation oncology consults.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 5/2/2026, discharged 5/5/2026.

Diagnoses: metastatic squamous cell lung carcinoma to brain, multiple lesions with vasogenic edema; new-onset seizure.

Hospital course: started levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily and dexamethasone 4 mg twice daily. No further seizures. Headache improved by day 2 and word-finding was better on discharge. Radiation oncology recommends stereotactic radiosurgery, simulation done, treatment 5/14. Medical oncology to continue docetaxel after radiosurgery.

Discharge medications: levetiracetam 500 mg BID (new); dexamethasone 4 mg BID with taper to be directed by radiation oncology (new); lisinopril 20 mg daily; hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily; atorvastatin 40 mg daily; aspirin 81 mg daily; tiotropium; albuterol as needed.

Instructions: no driving; seizure precautions; call for any further seizure.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; radiation oncology 5/14; medical oncology 5/19.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM. Discharge summary reviewed (received 5/7).

Admitted 5/2-5/5 after a first seizure at home; MRI showed several brain metastases with swelling. On levetiracetam 500 BID and dexamethasone 4 BID. Radiosurgery Thursday 5/14.

Since home: no further seizures. Headache much less. Wife says his words are coming easier; he agrees, still loses a word now and then. No falls. Not driving; we discussed that Massachusetts requires 6 months seizure-free before he drives again, and his wife will drive.

Exam: alert, conversational, mild word-finding pauses. No focal weakness, gait steady. Lungs diminished. No edema.

A/P
- Brain metastases with seizure. Levetiracetam continued; dexamethasone taper per radiation oncology. Checking glucose and potassium on the steroid.
- NSCLC: docetaxel to resume after SRS.
- Goals: he wants to keep treating. Offered to revisit planning conversation from last year at the next visit, wife grateful.
- Seizure precautions reviewed: no driving, no ladders, showers rather than baths.

Stereotactic radiosurgery delivered 5/14/2026 to the brain metastases identified on MRI 5/2/2026, single fraction, frameless mask immobilization. Treatment was well tolerated without acute side effects.

Plan: dexamethasone taper over 3 weeks per the attached schedule. Levetiracetam to continue. Follow-up MRI brain in 3 months (mid-August). Medical oncology resumes systemic therapy.
